package_info.package_versions: Versions prior to the patched release disclosed on March 7, 2017 (e.g., Struts 2.3.5–2.3.31, 2.5–2.5.10)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of Apache Struts contained a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2017-5638) that allowed attackers to execute arbitrary code on servers running vulnerable Struts applications. This vulnerability was publicly disclosed and widely exploited, enabling attackers to gain full control of affected systems, as seen in major breaches such as the Equifax incident.

execution_context.trigger: HTTP request processing (when Content-Type header or request parameters are parsed by the Struts framework)
execution_context.file_location: Core Struts framework classes responsible for processing OGNL expressions in request parameters (e.g., org.apache.struts2.dispatcher.Dispatcher, org.apache.struts2.interceptor.StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter)
required_permissions: process execution (to run system commands via OGNL injection)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The vulnerability allowed attackers to inject malicious OGNL expressions into HTTP request parameters or headers (such as Content-Type). The Struts framework would then evaluate these expressions without proper sanitization, resulting in arbitrary code execution. For example, an attacker could send a request with a header like: Content-Type: %{(#_='multipart/form-data').(#dm=@ognl.OgnlContext@DEFAULT_MEMBER_ACCESS).(#cmd='id').(#iswin=(@java.lang.System@getProperty('os.name').toLowerCase().contains('win'))).(#cmds=(#iswin?{'cmd.exe','/c',#cmd}:{'/bin/bash','-c',#cmd})).(#p=new java.lang.ProcessBuilder(#cmds)).(#p.redirectErrorStream(true)).(#process=#p.start()).(#ros=(@org.apache.struts2.ServletActionContext@getResponse().getOutputStream())).(@org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils@copy(#process.getInputStream(),#ros)).(#ros.flush())}
malicious_snippets.code_language: Java (OGNL expression injection via HTTP headers/parameters)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Processes attacker-supplied OGNL expressions embedded in HTTP request headers or parameters. The framework evaluates these expressions as code, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary system commands on the server with the privileges of the web application process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: User-supplied data, such as HTTP headers or parameters, should never be evaluated as executable code. The framework's failure to properly restrict OGNL expression evaluation allowed attackers to inject and execute arbitrary Java code, leading to full system compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior: HTTP request parameters and headers are treated strictly as data and never executed. Malicious behavior: The framework evaluates user-controlled OGNL expressions as code, allowing attackers to run arbitrary system commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Expression languages like OGNL are legitimately used for safe, limited dynamic content rendering within templates, but should never allow direct execution of system-level commands or unrestricted access to Java classes from user input.
key_indicators: OGNL expression evaluation triggered by user-supplied HTTP headers or parameters
Lack of input sanitization or restriction on OGNL expressions
Presence of system command execution patterns (e.g., java.lang.ProcessBuilder) in evaluated expressions
Web application logs showing OGNL payloads in HTTP requests
Unexpected invocation of sensitive Java classes (e.g., java.lang.Runtime, java.lang.ProcessBuilder) from request context

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request to a vulnerable Struts endpoint, embedding a malicious OGNL expression in a header (such as Content-Type) or request parameter.
attack_chain.leads_to: The OGNL expression is parsed and evaluated by the Struts framework during request processing.

attack_chain.action: The evaluated OGNL expression executes arbitrary Java code, such as invoking java.lang.ProcessBuilder to run system commands with the privileges of the web server process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves remote code execution on the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker leverages code execution to exfiltrate sensitive data, install malware, create backdoors, or pivot further into the internal network.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data breach, persistent compromise, or lateral movement within the organization.

behavioral_signatures: Evaluation of OGNL expressions from user-supplied HTTP headers or parameters
Execution of system commands (e.g., spawning shell processes) originating from the web application process
Web server logs containing OGNL payloads or suspicious Java class references in request data
Unusual or unauthorized file creation or modification by the web server process
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable Struts JAR files (e.g., struts2-core-2.3.5.jar, struts2-core-2.3.31.jar, struts2-core-2.5.10.jar) in application deployments
Web application logs showing OGNL expressions or suspicious Java code in HTTP request headers or parameters
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with OGNL payloads in headers (e.g., Content-Type) or parameters
Outbound network connections from web servers to external IPs or domains following exploitation
Unusual traffic patterns from web servers, such as connections to known command-and-control infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor web application and server logs for OGNL expressions or suspicious Java code in HTTP request headers and parameters. Scan deployed applications for known vulnerable Struts JAR versions. Alert on unexpected system command execution or process spawning by the web server process. Monitor for outbound network connections from web servers to untrusted destinations after suspicious requests. Use vulnerability scanners to identify unpatched Struts components and prioritize remediation.
